profile.note: Verified runtime baseline: the global dsh host runs @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.2.2-rc.1 and serves @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools 0.2.2-rc.1 to plugins through its installation-scope resolution, and 0.2.2-rc.1 IS published to the npm registry, so the build-against line now equals the runtime line. peerDependencies remain "*" so the host loads the plugin on any future line. Compatibility is decided ONLY by peerDependencies named "@deepseek-ai/dsh" or starting with "@deepseek-ai/dsh-" (semver.satisfies(runtime, range, {includePrerelease:true})); dependencies are never consulted.

knownIssues.summary: Two schemastery copies in one program break the `z<Config>` annotation
knownIssues.detail: @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools pins its own schemastery range. If the plugin's own copy is a different version, the program contains two Schema types and the Config annotation fails with TS2322. The profile currently serves schemastery 3.18.5 while this repo typechecks against 3.18.5-alpha.1; keep the plugin copy on the same build-against line and re-run typecheck after any host bump.
knownIssues.resolution: Keep @deepseek-ai/schemastery equal to the version the pinned @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools depends on, and re-run pnpm typecheck after any host-line bump.

knownIssues.summary: A narrow @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools peer range makes the host refuse the plugin
knownIssues.detail: The host skips a bundle whose @deepseek-ai/dsh-* peer ranges do not satisfy the running dsh version ('is incompatible with dsh <version>'), and it never consults dependencies. package.json peerDependencies['@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'] must therefore stay '*' (the toolchain gate enforces it).
knownIssues.resolution: Never narrow the dsh peer range; express the build-against line in devDependencies + this manifest instead, and run pnpm verify:host-compat after a host update.
